C-UPDATER-NET-BOUNDS.Name: Bounded, serialized forward-update path — implementation plan
C-UPDATER-NET-BOUNDS.IntentSummary: Implement the approved spec in seven sequential tasks in the green-upd1 worktree, no product behavior beyond R-1..R-8: (T-001→T-002 renderer) the shared install flow installSignedUpdate carries named deadlines through the plugin's own timeout seams — check({ timeout: UPDATER_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS }) with UPDATER_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000 and update.downloadAndInstall(undefined, { timeout: UPDATER_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS }) with UPDATER_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS = 300_000 (the zone's rollback fetch-deadline parity, ROLLBACK_FETCH_DEADLINE_SECS = 300, m068_rollback.rs:129); a module-scope single-flight guard (installInFlight) makes a second overlapping invocation an explicit localized refusal that invokes nothing and re-arms after the live attempt settles; the progress toast names update.version from the flow's own fresh re-check and status.latestVersion leaves every user-visible string; the terminal failure surfaces exactly one localized notice (new updater.failureTitle/Body keys) with the raw error demoted to the console marker; (T-003) the four updater.* keys land in all ten locales gated by tests/renderer/i18n/locale-keys.test.js; (T-004→T-005 Rust) mt_updater_check builds through UpdaterBuilder::timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(UPDATER_CHECK_TIMEOUT_SECS)) with UPDATER_CHECK_TIMEOUT_SECS = 15 preserving the Err→statusNote squash, and prepare becomes idempotent: a root-explicit prepare_inner_at(root, bundle) seam (the load_valid_live_at convention) reuses an intact staging set of the running version (schema + previous_version == running + platform + digest re-verification — the mirrored inverse of validate's rollback-to-self rejection at :288-290, deliberately NOT routed through load_valid_live, whose validate() would reject exactly that set) and wipes-and-reprepares on any other state, keeping mt_rollback_prepare's spawn_blocking body and the fail-closed ordering untouched — discharging the F-008 cut; (T-006) the mandatory Rust backup-channel stand: the real plugin over a controlled local two-endpoint fixture (hung primary → mirror latest.json → a gateway-imitating /pkg route serving minisign-verified payload bytes) driven through UpdaterBuilder's endpoint/pubkey/timeout/target seams on a tauri::test mock app, zero external network, proving the package bytes arrive via the feed-carried URL under the builder deadline; (T-007) the e2e freshness scenario over plugin:updater|* shim handlers plus the graph/verification deltas (M-016/M-068 SummaryDelta, V-M-016/V-M-068 scenarios+commands) and the VERSION/CHANGE_SUMMARY sync. T-002.Title: Renderer implementation: timeout plumbing, module-scope single-flight, fresh-data toasts, localized failure classes — inside START_BLOCK_INSTALL_SIGNED_UPDATE only

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Deadline constants with the spec's justification in comments, named exactly: const UPDATER_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000 (metadata-only latest.json feed, per-request bound, the two-endpoint sweep worst case ≈ 30 s tolerated by the 24 h launch check and turned into bounded feedback on the manual path; the rollback connect-deadline mirror at m068 :125) and const UPDATER_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS = 300_000 (the plugin's whole-request bound covering connect+headers+body; sized for the ~31 MB Windows installer / ~14 MB macOS archive at ≈ 1 Mbit/s ≈ 248 s — the ROLLBACK_FETCH_DEADLINE_SECS parity, m068 :129); before pinning, the implementer re-measures the current release artifact sizes (the shipped latest.json / release assets) and records the measured numbers in the constant's comment — a measurement that contradicts the 300 s justification is a recorded deviation, never a silent value change. The only plugin-call shapes: const update = await check({ timeout: UPDATER_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS }) and await update.downloadAndInstall(undefined, { timeout: UPDATER_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS }) — no headers, no proxy, no URL material anywhere in the flow (F-UPDATER-PROGRESS-UI stays out; no onEvent callback is added).

Module-scope single-flight in commands/index.js (outside the command array; both the file.check-update entry and the notice's INSTALL_UPDATE converge on installSignedUpdate by construction): let installInFlight = null; on entry, if (installInFlight) the flow surfaces exactly one localized refusal (title t('updater.inProgressTitle'), body t('updater.inProgressBody')), logs a console marker, invokes nothing (no second mt_rollback_prepare, no check, no downloadAndInstall) and returns; otherwise the whole body (prepare → check → download → relaunch / up-to-date) runs under installInFlight, which clears to null when the attempt settles (success or failure) so a retry works as today; the prepare-failure early return also clears the guard. Cross-window residual recorded, not built: the Settings window's General tab (prefComponents/tabs/general/index.vue :277-288, read-only) is a second webview context with its own module instance — the guard serializes all entries within each context, and cross-context overlap is re-established at a Rust-level choke point only if it ever matters (the spec's recorded escalation path; the plugin command stays untouched).

Fresh-data toasts (R-6): the progress toast names update.version from the re-check that actually drives the install — `Updating to Mark ${update.version}…`; the up-to-date branch keeps `Mark ${status.currentVersion} is up to date` (the running version cannot change within a session); status.latestVersion no longer reaches any user-visible string (pinned by T-001's fresh-recheck test and the MustNotContain target pin); INSTALL_UPDATE's handoff shape is unchanged (store/autoUpdates.js read-only, expected diff: none).

Localized failure states (R-4, the C-SEARCH-ERROR-VISIBILITY voice): the shared flow's terminal catch surfaces exactly one notice with title t('updater.failureTitle') and body t('updater.failureBody'); the raw error string goes only to a console.error marker in the file's BLOCK convention (e.g. [commands][install][BLOCK_INSTALL_FAILED]) and never into the notify payload; nothing renders a deadline exhaustion as «is up to date»; the manual path's English catch (:1375-1377) and statusNote rendering stay as they are.

The START_BLOCK_INSTALL_SIGNED_UPDATE / END_BLOCK_INSTALL_SIGNED_UPDATE pair stays unique and load-bearing; commands/index.js gets its VERSION bump + CHANGE_SUMMARY entry recording the four changes and the F-008 renderer half-discharge; the C-66/C-UPDATER-ROLLBACK ordering/cancel pins and tests/renderer/store/autoUpdates.test.js stay green unweakened.

T-006.Title: The mandatory backup-channel stand: the real plugin over a local two-endpoint fixture — hung primary, mirror latest.json, gateway-imitating package route — zero external network

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: A dedicated #[cfg(all(test, not(feature = "app-store")))] mod updater_backup_channel in m016_updater.rs drives the real tauri-plugin-updater over a controlled local fixture: a std::net::TcpListener bound to 127.0.0.1:0 in a spawned thread serving hand-rolled HTTP/1.1 with three routes — GET /feed-hang (the failing primary: accepted, never answered), GET /latest.json (the mirror: a static manifest {"version": "999.0.0", "platforms": {"test-target": {"url": "http://127.0.0.1:<port>/pkg/darwin-aarch64/999.0.0", "signature": <fixture signature>}}} carrying the package URL exactly as a real feed does), GET /pkg/... (the gateway-imitating route serving the fixture payload bytes) — with every request line recorded into a shared mutex Vec for the evidence assertions; the fixture minisign constants (throwaway keypair + the signature of the fixture payload) are embedded as constants generated at implementation time with the tauri signer CLI (the plugin's own offline_tests precedent, updater.rs :2117-2123); no new dependency (Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock untouched — tauri[test], tempfile and tokio are already dev-deps) and no external network (the test fails if the recorded request log contains anything but 127.0.0.1 routes).

The stand registers the plugin on a tauri::test mock app (updater_builder() requires the registered plugin state — the state<UpdaterState> read at lib.rs :79-88) and drives only the plugin's own injectable UpdaterBuilder seams: handle.updater_builder().endpoints(vec![primary, mirror]).unwrap().target("test-target").pubkey(<fixture pubkey>).timeout(Duration::from_secs(15)).build().unwrap().check().await must deliver Ok(Some(update)) from the MIRROR despite the hung primary (the failover loop, updater.rs :545-658), with the elapsed time ≥ the builder timeout on the primary so the deadline provably engaged rather than instant-failed; update.download(...) then fetches and verifies the payload (Update::download verifies the fetched bytes, updater.rs :891); the recorded request log is asserted to show the package bytes served on the feed-carried /pkg route — the Wave-4 criterion "for the backup channel, verify obtaining the package itself" discharged with the real plugin and no stand-in; the named test (backup_feed_channel_delivers_the_package_via_the_feed_carried_url_under_the_deadline) stays inside the m016_updater:: filter.

The seam-failure escape hatch is named, never silent: if a concrete tauri::test/plugin seam proves unusable (e.g. the mock runtime rejects the plugin's macOS main-thread dispatch), the downgrade is admissible only as an individually justified, explicitly recorded gap in the V-M-016 scenario (the exact failing seam + the retained evidence: the JS timeout pins, the URL-as-is pins, the installed-plugin source citation for the failover loop) per the spec's Backup-channel criterion — never a blanket or silent fallback.

T-007.Title: e2e freshness scenario over plugin:updater|* shim handlers, graph and verification deltas, governance sync

AcceptanceVerification.Environment: Execution is strictly sequential T-001→T-007 in the green-upd1 worktree (single-writer per file; the renderer track T-001..T-003, the Rust track T-004..T-006, governance last). Environment prerequisites the orchestrator/implementer runs — this plan does not: `npm ci` FIRST (the worktree has no node_modules; every vitest/playwright gate depends on it); cargo rides the existing offline cache, and the root Cargo.lock present in the tree pins tauri-plugin-updater 2.14.1 so every cargo gate keeps --locked --offline (the spec's "no Cargo.lock" assumption is recorded as outdated in ReferenceState). Failing-first semantics: T-001's renderer pins exit red with recorded receipts (green at T-002), T-004's m016 pins fail at runtime and the m068 pins fail to compile before T-005 (the honest red for a not-yet-existing seam) — both receipts recorded. The Rust stand binds 127.0.0.1 only and fails on any non-loopback request; its fixture signing constants are generated at implementation time with the tauri signer CLI and embedded as constants. The C-66 e2e matrix, the C-UPDATER-ROLLBACK ordering/cancel pins, the manual-path English catch pin, the m068 deadline/accounting suites and the app-store stub suites keep their bodies green and unweakened. grace lint runs only in the external lifecycle gates (current before editing — recorded as the pre-change baseline; target during implementation; final --run-commands before handoff) — this plan deliberately carries no self-referential grace-lint command, and the orchestrator pins SpecSha256 at admission (`shasum -a 256 .grace/changes/active/C-UPDATER-NET-BOUNDS/spec.xml`). All gates pass with no skips, retries, budget increases or weakened assertions; no apply/archive, commit/push, version release, tag or publication is authorized by this plan.
